transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is that my head just feels kind of foggy lately. I've been making these little mistakes in my client notes at work, or, uh, just forgetting what I was about to do right in the middle of doing it. It really isn't like me to be this scattered, so I figured I should come see someone.
Did this fogginess start after a stressful event or major change in your life?
Yeah, actually. My uncle died about two weeks ago, and that's really when I noticed this whole shift starting.
Since your uncle died, have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah, I have. Lately I just wake up with this... heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. I mean, I can still get through my shift and talk to my clients and everything, but inside, I'm just feeling really sad and... flat, I guess.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Not really, no. I still like doing my usual stuff when I get off work. I still watch my shows and, you know, tinker around the house. It's just... I guess I just have that sad feeling in the background while I'm doing it. But I wouldn't say I've lost interest in them.
Have you been feeling unusually anxious or worried lately?
No, not really. I mean, I'm sad about my uncle, obviously, but I'm not feeling extra anxious or worried about anything in particular. Just... just the sadness, mostly.
Have you been having trouble remembering recent conversations or appointments?

Yeah, actually, I have. My head just feels kind of... foggy lately. I've been making these little mistakes in my client notes at work, or I'll just completely forget what I was about to do right after I thought of it. It's really not like me to do that.
Did these memory problems start only after your uncle died?
Yeah, it did. This whole shift... the foggy head, the sadness, all of it... it really just started after he passed away. That was about two weeks ago.
Since your uncle died, have you been feeling hopeless?

I don't know if I'd use the word hopeless, exactly, but... yeah, it's been really hard. Lately I just wake up with this heavy, empty feeling in my chest. I mean, I can still get through my shift and talk to people fine, but inside I'm just... sad and flat.
Have these symptoms been making it hard for you to do your job or handle things at home?

Yeah, a little bit. At work, I've actually started asking my coworkers to double-check my client documentation for me before I turn it in. And at home... well, my wife has taken over some of the bills and the scheduling lately. I'm just... I'm just not as reliable with those kinds of details right now.
Since your uncle died, have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, I have. Like I said earlier, my head just feels really foggy. I'm making these little mistakes in my client notes at work, or I'll just... forget what I was about to do right in the middle of a task. It's really not like me to be this scattered.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day, nearly every day, since your uncle died?

Yeah, pretty much. Like I mentioned a minute ago, it's just this heavy, empty feeling in my chest that starts right when I wake up. It's there most of the time. I can still smile and talk to my clients, but underneath all that, it's just... sad and flat all day.
Since your uncle died, have you stopped enjoying the things you usually like to do?

Not really, no. I still like doing my usual stuff. I mean, I might feel heavy or sad like I was just saying, but if I sit down to watch a game or work out in the yard, I still get enjoyment out of it. I haven't really lost interest in my hobbies or anything.
Since your uncle died, has your appetite changed?
No, not really. I'm still eating about the same as usual. I haven't noticed any changes with my appetite, to be honest.
Since your uncle died, have you had any thoughts that life isn’t worth living or that you’d be better off dead?

Well, I'm definitely not planning to hurt myself or anything like that. But... yeah, I guess there have been a few mornings lately where I wake up and just think, you know, it wouldn't be the worst thing in the world if I just hadn't woken up at all. It's not like I want to die, but having those thoughts... it definitely scares me a little bit.
Since your uncle died, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty?

Yeah, I have. I just keep replaying what I should have done for my tío before he passed. Like, I think about how I should have called him more often, or made the time to visit him sooner. I just end up feeling like I really failed him as family.
Since your uncle died, have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, my sleep has been pretty messed up lately. I'll just lie there in bed, you know, thinking about all that family stuff and what I should have done. Or sometimes I'll wake up way before my alarm goes off, and I just can't seem to settle back down and get any more rest.
Since your uncle died, have you been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?
No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I think I'm moving and talking about the same as I usually do. My family or friends haven't pointed out anything like that, either.
Since your uncle died, have you been feeling unusually tired or like you have less energy than usual?

Yeah, I definitely have. It's like, even on days when I really don't do much, my body just feels completely worn out. Simple things are just... they're harder right now. Like helping one of my clients take a shower at work, or even just carrying the groceries into the house—it all just takes way more out of me than it normally should.
Since your uncle died, have you been feeling like you are a worthless person?

I don't know about the word worthless, exactly, but... yeah, I've been dealing with a lot of guilt. I just keep replaying what I should have done for my tío before he died. Like, I should have called him more often, or made the trip to visit him sooner. I just end up feeling like I really failed him as family.
Does your sadness tend to come in waves when something reminds you of your uncle?

No, I wouldn't really say it comes in waves. It's not really tied to specific reminders, you know? It's just... kind of a steady sadness that's just there most of the time right now, no matter what I'm doing.
